title: Factorization of the absolute Frobenius
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $p$ is prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k$ is a fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$. Let $X_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. As in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], let $\sigma:k\to k$ be $b\mapsto b^q$, put $g_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$, and let $\Phi=\Phi_0\times\operatorname{id}_k$, where $\Phi_0$ is the absolute $q$-power Frobenius of $X_0$. For every integer $m\geq1$, the absolute $q^m$-power Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]
$\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X:X\to X$, whose affine incarnation on the base change of any affine chart $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0\subseteq X_0$ is $u\otimes b\mapsto u^{q^m}\otimes b^{q^m}$, factors as an equality of $k_0$-scheme morphisms

$$
\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X=g_\sigma^m\circ\Phi^m=\Phi^m\circ g_\sigma^m.
$$

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text: Take the affine charts $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ of $X_0$ and their geometric base changes $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A_0\otimes_{k_0}k)$, on which [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] gives the affine incarnations of $\Phi$ and $g_\sigma$. These charts cover $X$ and are preserved by both maps: $g_\sigma$ lies over the identity of $X_0$, while $\Phi_0$ is identity on the underlying space by [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. On $B=A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ write their ring maps as $P(u\otimes b)=u^q\otimes b$ and $S(u\otimes b)=u\otimes b^q$. Induction gives $P^m(u\otimes b)=u^{q^m}\otimes b$ and $S^m(u\otimes b)=u\otimes b^{q^m}$: for $m=0$ both are identities; composing once more replaces the exponent $q^m$ by $q^m q=q^{m+1}$.

source.place: Proof, affine incarnations on the two factors; expanded iteration and chart restriction. Absolute Frobenius is Stacks tag 03SM (varieties.tex, definition-absolute-frobenius).

proof.text:
On a pure tensor the two ring-map composites satisfy
$$S^mP^m(u\otimes b)=u^{q^m}\otimes b^{q^m}=P^mS^m(u\otimes b).$$
This is also $(u\otimes b)^{q^m}$, since multiplication in the tensor-product algebra multiplies the two factors. The $q^m=p^{am}$ power map $H$ on $B$ is a ring homomorphism by [def-weil-ring-frobenius]. The formulas for $P,S$ used here are those of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] (a scalar multiplying a pure tensor is absorbed in its first factor). Additivity therefore gives, for $t=\sum_i u_i\otimes b_i$,
$$S^mP^m(t)=\sum_i u_i^{q^m}\otimes b_i^{q^m}=H(t)=P^mS^m(t).$$
Thus the two composites equal $H$ on the entire ring, including its nilpotent elements.

source.place: Proof, composition in either order; expanded pure-tensor and finite-sum computation. Stacks tag 03SM (varieties.tex, definition-absolute-frobenius) for the power map.

proof.text: The absolute $q^m$-power Frobenius restricts on $U$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(H)$ by [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Contravariance and uniqueness in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] turn Step 2 into equality of its restriction with both $g_\sigma^m\circ\Phi^m$ and $\Phi^m\circ g_\sigma^m$ on $U$. This proves the global equality: the underlying continuous maps agree on the covering charts, hence at every point; their maps on structure sheaves then agree locally on those charts, so agree on any open by the uniqueness clause of the sheaf axiom. These are exactly the two data of a scheme morphism in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. The maps are over $k_0$ by their construction in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], so the same equalities hold as $k_0$-scheme morphisms.

source.place: Proof, final equality of morphisms from affine incarnations. Affine uniqueness: Stacks tag 01I1 (schemes.tex, lemma-morphism-into-affine); morphism data: tags 0091 (sheaves.tex, definition-ringed-space) and 01HB (schemes.tex, definition-locally-ringed-space).
